content: Tinidazole should be taken with food to reduce the likelihood of epigastric discomfort and other gastrointestinal side effects. The presence of food does not affect the oral bioavailability of tinidazole. Alcoholic beverages must be avoided during tinidazole therapy and for three days after completing the treatment. For patients who cannot swallow tablets, tinidazole tablets can be crushed and mixed with artificial cherry syrup to create an oral suspension, which should also be taken with food. To prepare this suspension, four 500 mg tinidazole tablets should be pulverized using a mortar and pestle. Approximately 10 mL of cherry syrup should then be added to the powder and mixed until smooth. The resulting suspension should be transferred to a graduated amber container. Any remaining drug in the mortar should be rinsed with small amounts of cherry syrup and added to the final suspension to achieve a total volume of 30 mL. This suspension is stable for up to seven days at room temperature and must be shaken well before each administration. For the treatment of trichomoniasis, the recommended dose for both males and females is a single 2 g oral dose taken with food. Since trichomoniasis is a sexually transmitted infection, sexual partners should also be treated with the same dose at the same time. For giardiasis, the recommended dose in adults is a single 2 g oral dose taken with food. In pediatric patients older than three years, the recommended dose is a single dose of 50 mg/kg (up to a maximum of 2 g) taken with food. For intestinal amebiasis, the recommended dose in adults is 2 g per day for three days, taken with food. In pediatric patients older than three years, the recommended dose is 50 mg/kg/day (up to a maximum of 2 g per day) for three days, taken with food. For amebic liver abscess, the recommended dose in adults is 2 g per day for three to five days, taken with food. In pediatric patients older than three years, the recommended dose is 50 mg/kg/day (up to a maximum of 2 g per day) for three to five days, taken with food. There is limited pediatric data on treatment durations exceeding three days, although a small number of children have been treated for five days without additional reported adverse reactions. For bacterial vaginosis in non-pregnant females, the recommended dose is either a 2 g oral dose once daily for two days or a 1 g oral dose once daily for five days, both taken with food. The use of tinidazole in pregnant patients for bacterial vaginosis has not been studied.
